messages.subject: scale / legend question
parts:
In the following example, discount has been generated so that it will
always be divisible by 10. So, I would like the legend for discount to
show (10,20,30,40,...). When I run the example as shown below, I get
my preferred output; however, when I use max=4 when generating
discount, the legend is broken up as (10,15,20,25,30,...). How can I
ensure that the discount alpha values are grouped in multiples of 10?

==============================
df <- data.frame(
sid = c(rep('11',30),rep('22',30)),
time = rep(ISOdate(year=2010, month = 1, day = 1:30), 2),
sales = c(rnorm(30,1000,20), rnorm(30,900,10)),
discount = round(runif(60,0, max=5))*10
)

df <- merge(df, aggregate(df$sales, by=list(sid=df$sid), max),
by="sid", all.x=TRUE)
colnames(df)[5] <- "max.sales"

ggplot(df) + theme_bw() +
geom_line(aes(time, sales), size=1) +
geom_point(data=subset(df,discount>5), aes(time, max.sales,
alpha=discount)) +
facet_wrap(~sid, nrow=2, scales='free_y')

df$discount
==============================

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: scale / legend question
parts:
Hi:

You could make discount a factor and create the levels using the cut()
function, as follows:

df$Discount <- factor(cut(df2$discount, c(-1, 10, 20, 30, 40, 50)),
                               labels = c('10', '20', '30', '40', '50'))

If you do that, then the plot call is modified as follows, since Discount is a factor:

geom_point(aes(time, max.sales, alpha = I(as.numeric(Discount)/100))) +
  facet_wrap(~sid, nrow=2, scales='free_y') +
  scale_alpha("discount", breaks = seq(0.01, 0.05, by = 0.01),
              labels = c('10', '20', '30', '40', '50'))

BTW, an easier way to aggregate/merge is to use ddply() with transform.
I did the following prior to defining the Discount variable; taking df to be
defined as in your code below,

df2 <- ddply(df, .(sid), transform, max.sales = max(sales))
> identical(df, df2)
[1] TRUE

HTH,
Dennis
